title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from the previous page). I is a poset and Φ = (X_i)_{i∈I} is a family of subsets of a set X. Put ∂X_i = ∪_{j<i} X_j, X_i° = X_i \ ∂X_i, |Φ| = ∪ X_i, and I^x = {i : x ∈ X_i}. Then x ∈ X_i° iff i is a minimal element of I^x.

The proposition lists equivalent conditions:
(i) every I^x (x ∈ |Φ|) has a least element.
(ii) every I^x has a minimal element, and X_i ∩ X_j = ∪_{k≤i,j} X_k.
(iii) a) the X_i° are pairwise disjoint; b) X_i = ∪_{j≤i} X_j°.
(iv) with I' = {i : X_i° ≠ ∅}: α) (X_i°)_{i∈I'} is a partition of |Φ|; β) each X_i is saturated for this partition; γ) for X_j° ≠ ∅, X_j° ⊂ X_i implies j ≤ i.

This page proves (i) ⇔ (iii) and starts on (iv).
- A subset of a poset has a least element iff three things hold: (1°) it has a minimal element; (2°) any two minimal elements are equal; (3°) every element lies above some minimal element. The margin correctly notes that 3° implies 1°, since I^x is nonempty.
- Quantified over x, these become: 1') |Φ| = ∪ X_i°; 2') i ≠ j implies X_i° ∩ X_j° = ∅; 3') X_i = ∪_{j≤i} X_j°.
- Since |Φ| = ∪ X_i, 3') implies 1'. Hence (i) ⇔ 2') + 3'), which are exactly a), b).
- He then translates α) into 1'') (equivalent to 1') and into disjointness over I' (equivalent to 2'). The next page completes the argument: (iv) ⇔ (i) + γ, and (i) ⇒ γ via Corollary 1.

Margins ask whether β) and γ) follow from α) when I is finite, and whether 2') implies 1'); both are answered 'no, cf. p. 44'.

Modern reading. Under (i) the rule x ↦ min I^x defines a map s: |Φ| → I. When Φ is monotone, X_i = s⁻¹(I_{≤i}), the X_i° are the strata s⁻¹(i), and the X_i are the closed (down-set) pieces. This is the set-theoretic core of a poset-indexed stratification, which Grothendieck is setting up for his 'Analysis situs' treatment of stratified spaces. He reworks prop. 1 of an earlier chapter ('CF V') in an 'indexed' setting.
errors: Proving 3') as an equality X_i = ∪_{j≤i} X_j° needs X_j ⊂ X_i for j ≤ i, i.e. monotonicity of Φ. Pointwise 3° only gives the inclusion X_i ⊂ ∪_{j≤i} X_j°. The previous page writes ∂X_i ⊂ X_i (implicitly assuming monotonicity), while a margin note there and the next page ('on n'a pas supposé que i≤j ⇒ X_i⊂X_j ?!') show Grothendieck noticed the ambiguity. Without monotonicity, (i) ⇒ 3') as an equality is not justified.
Labelling slip: the conditions a), b) appear in (iii), yet the conclusion is written as '(i) ⟺ (ii)' (reading of the image uncertain). What is actually proved is (i) ⟺ (iii).
The remark 'automatique si I fini' for 1') and 3') really only needs I to be well-founded (every nonempty subset has a minimal element). Finiteness is sufficient but not necessary; this is minor.

ideas.what: A family of subsets indexed by a poset in which each point has a least index; the strata X_i° = X_i minus the union of lower X_j form a partition, and the X_i are unions of strata (preimages of down-sets).
ideas.modern_name: Poset-stratified set/space, i.e. a stratification map s: X → P with closed pieces s⁻¹(P_{≤p})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical stratification theory (Whitney, Thom, Mather); the formulation as a map to a poset with the Alexandrov topology is common in modern treatments (e.g. Lurie, Higher Algebra, Appendix A).
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (§5–6, 'topologie modérée', stratified structures) discusses stratifications informally; this lemma itself does not appear there.

ideas.what: Decomposing 'least element exists' into: a minimal element exists, minimal elements are unique, and every element dominates a minimal one; then translating each pointwise statement into set identities.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine set-theoretic lemma about poset-indexed families of subsets and their strata, preparing the stratified 'Analysis situs'. It is correct up to an implicit monotonicity assumption, which Grothendieck himself flags on the next page. Nothing here is new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: '|𝓛|' should be read as '|Φ|' (the notation of the previous page).

'Dém. La condition 1(i)' is probably 'La condition (i)' or a reference to the proposition's (i). The later 'a), b) de 1(ii)' should refer to a), b) of (iii); the image may read '(iii)' or Grothendieck slipped.
'X_j^0' and 'X_i^0' should be read as X_j°, X_i° (strata, 'ouvert' notation).
In γ), the image reads 'X_j° ⊂ X_i ⟹ j ≤ i', with the inserted hypothesis 'et X_j° ≠ ∅'.
